g3ela-18-2-teach-morph: When you see a long word, find the part at the start first, then read the rest. Tap a word in the game, then tap what it means. If you're stuck, look at the first part of the word. It gives you a big clue.
g3ela-18-2-teach-gram: Joining words are back, and today you're a joining-word spotter. In each sentence, first tap the joining word. Then tap the part of the sentence that comes after it. That part is the new idea the joining word brings in. Last, pick one sentence and write it again with a different joining word. Notice how the meaning changes.
g3ela-18-2-teach-spell: Let's go hunting for vowel teams. Read the two sentences slowly. Every time you see two vowels working together, tap that word. There's more than one, so keep looking until the game says you found them all.
g3ela-18-3-teach-spell: Here's today's rule: when you split a word into syllables, never split the team. The team always stays together. Rain, bow. Sea, son. Look at each word, find the vowel team, and think about where the split goes. Then tap the word to check.
g3ela-18-4-teach-gram: Today you're the teacher, checking someone else's work. Some of these sentences use the wrong joining word. Read each sentence out loud. If the joining word doesn't match the meaning, tap it. If the sentence is right, tap No mistake. Then tell which sentence had no mistake, and how you knew.
g3ela-18-4-teach-spell: Let's roll some vowel team words. Tap Roll the dice. When a word comes up, say it out loud and clap the syllables. Find the vowel team, and remember, the team never splits. Meadow: mead, ow. Then tap Check my answer to see if you split it the right way.
g3ela-18-2-teach-vocab: Let's be word detectives again. Here's astonishment. Read the sentence: Jemmy stared at him with dreadful astonishment. Jemmy just heard something he never expected. Now look at the parts. Astonish means to surprise, and ment turns it into a thing. So astonishment is a feeling of great surprise.
g3ela-18-4-teach-vocab: This week you met lots of new words. Today you'll use four of them. Let's start with contrite. The prince lowered his head so as to appear humbled and contrite. He's trying to look sorry. So contrite means truly sorry for something you did wrong. Fill in each sentence from the word bank, then tap Check My Work.
